title: Lacuna sweep: 2025-26 ML papers on multi-agent accountability, attribution, rollback
outcome: Find the most relevant recent papers, research directions and open hypotheses in Lacuna that our Sprint 1 web research missed
acceptance: uses Lacuna search_lacuna (paper, cluster, hypothesis, resource) with Lacuna URLs cited
≥8 relevant papers 2025-2026 with 1-line relevance each, ranked
names the closest competitor work to per-agent selective undo, with how we differ
linked code/datasets/benchmarks we could reuse for the 10-agent eval
summary:
Closest competitor is Airlock (arXiv 2611.06727, Nov 2026): provenance DAG + min-cut containment that keeps healthy work (+68 to +96 pp), but it contains, it does not undo landed effects. Our niche: containment + selective undo + tamper-evident audit.
Second closest: From Spark to Fire (2603.04474), lineage-graph rollback of messages only.
12 ranked 2025-26 papers; Who&When best step-level attribution 14.2% vs structured graph reading 55.2% (different splits), so a deterministic recorder beats LLM judges.
Lacuna has no hypothesis on per-agent selective undo; survey 2606.04990 names recovery-oriented evaluation as open.
No ready 10-agent fault-injection benchmark found: build our own, reuse Airlock/ARIA/Who&When metrics.
Caveat: papers read as Lacuna summaries; Airlock's July 2026 OpenAI-HF incident claim is unverified (RES-07).
